gloss: to be absent-minded; to space out; to be vague

definitions.gloss: to be absent-minded; to space out; to be in a daze
definitions.explanation: Describes a person whose mind is not focused — daydreaming, zoning out, or not paying attention.

definitions.gloss: to be vague; to be hazy; to be indistinct
definitions.explanation: Describes things that are unclear or blurry — outlines, memories, shapes seen through fog.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}の{外|そと}をぼんやり{眺|なが}めていた。
examples.english: I was gazing absent-mindedly out the window.

examples.japanese: {寝不足|ねぶそく}で{一日|いちにち}{中|じゅう}ぼんやりしていた。
examples.english: I was in a daze all day from lack of sleep.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}くの{山|やま}がぼんやり{見|み}える。
examples.english: The distant mountains are faintly visible.

examples.japanese: {記憶|きおく}がぼんやりしている。
{霧|きり}で{周|まわ}りの{景色|けしき}がぼんやりとしか{見|み}えなかった。
examples.english: Because of the fog, the surrounding scenery was only dimly visible.

notes:
An onomatopoeic word ({擬態語|ぎたいご}) that can function as a する verb or as an adverb. Very natural and common in everyday speech.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ぼんやりする: to zone out, be dazed
- ぼんやり（と）: as an adverb (vaguely, absent-mindedly)
- ぼんやりした{表情|ひょうじょう}: a vacant expression
- ぼんやりした{記憶|きおく}: a vague memory

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ぼーっとする: to space out (very close; slightly more colloquial)
- うっかりする: to be careless, do something absent-mindedly (implies a mistake)
- {曖昧|あいまい}な: ambiguous, vague (more formal, for statements or situations)
